thread.title: Dow Leads As Apple Reverses Higher; India Sends Bitcoin Crashing

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Dow Leads As Apple Reverses Higher; India Sends Bitcoin Crashing

organizations.name: spdr s&p oil & gas exploration & production

text:
Stocks rallied to gains Thursday after starting with steep early losses. Facebook ( FB ) rallied to a record high and Apple ( AAPL ) edged higher ahead of its earnings.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) led with a 0.5% gain, SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) advanced 0.4% and PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) climbed 0.1%. Emerging markets underperformed as iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) fell 0.5%.
Among sector plays, energy, financials and technology led the upside in the stock market today , while utilities, real estate and retail lagged. SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ( XOP ) picked up 0.4% to hold support at  . A solid rebound off the support line could present an opportunity to buy shares.
 
SPDR Technology ( XLK ) advanced 0.7% as it nears a new record high. Component stock Facebook surged nearly 4% to a new high after the social network's Q4 results topped views. It's now slightly extended from buy range. Apple edged 0.3% higher ahead of its quarterly earnings due after the close. Shares remain below the 50-day line and 6% off their high.
Bitcoin tumbled 11% to $9,007.55, according to CoinDesk , down from an earlier climb to $10,203.07. The cryptocurrency has been under pressure amid increased scrutiny and potential government crackdowns. India does not consider cryptocurrencies as a legal form of payment , the country's finance minister said, according to Bloomberg. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) gapped down and plunged 14%, on track for its lowest close in over two months.
Small-Cap Test? A small-cap-stock play holding the likes of Wolverine Worldwide ( WWW ) and SkyWest ( SKYW ) is getting ready to test   .
IShares S&P Small-Cap Value ( IJS ) could set up a potential buy opportunity if it pulls back to, then stages a solid rebound off, the support line. Shares rose 7% from a mid-December bounce off the 50-day to their Jan. 16 intraday high.
The fund, which tracks the index with the same name, has gathered $5.6 billion since its July 2000 launch. The index is composed of small-cap U.S. stocks that are considered undervalued vs. comparable peers.
Financials and industrials led the sector weightings as of Jan. 30, with each accounting for roughly 19% of assets. Consumer discretionary represented 16%, information technology 13%, and materials and energy about 7% apiece. Health care, real estate, utilities, consumer staples and telecommunications made up the rest.
Top holdings in the 451-stock portfolio included IT services provider CACI International ( CACI ), PDC Energy ( PDCE ), footwear maker Wolverine Worldwide, packaging products maker Kapstone Paper & Packaging ( KS ), and carrier SkyWest.
Most are performing in line with or lagging the broader market so far this year. But SkyWest and Wolverine outpaced the market last year with respective gains of 46% and 45%, more than doubling the S&P 500's 19% return. SkyWest has a 92 Relative Strength Rating; Wolverine's is 86. But their gains were tempered by underperformers.
